text.p: The sale of Banco di Napoli to Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and insurer INA could lead to the privatisation of the southern bank in a few years time, INA's chairman said.
"This has not been a privatisation, it has been a prelude to a privatisation," Sergio Siglienti told a news conference.
The Treasury will complete the transfer of control of Banco di Napoli on Wednesday to Banco Napoli Holding Spa, an acquisition vehicle in which INA holds 51 percent and BNL 49 percent.
Banco di Napoli made cumulative net losses of 5.797 trillion lire betwen 1994 and 1996 but is expected to break even this year.

"We think that breakeven is feasible in 1997 and that from 1998 it can start making a profit," said Siglienti, adding: "If in two to three years it reaches a good level of profitability then we can go private."
BNL is owned by the Treasury and INA has been only partly privatised, with 34.3 percent of its stock still in state hands, even though the Treasury retains voting rights on only five percent.
Siglienti said a strategic partner, possibly a foreign bank, would eventually be sought for Banco di Napoli.
Banco di Napoli's new owners also plan to appoint an adviser to draw up a master plan for the bank's strategic development.
A first capital increase of 900 billion lire in cash is planned for July to be followed by a second 400 billion lire increase, in cash or earning assets, within nine months.
The bank was believed to have 1,200 excess staff but lay-offs were proceeding at the rate of 200 a month, said Siglienti. --Milan newsroom +392-66102321
